source.title: Data-driven Regularization via Racecar Training for Generalizing Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: Tests a new data-driven regularization method on natural-image classification and reports held-out performance; the claim versions do not cover this method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's natural-label MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification results. Transfer tasks, stylization, generative tasks, and feature measurements do not test the listed versions or the training-to-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates racecar regularization and feature transfer. None of its comparisons tests V1–V8; improved held-out accuracy from a new regularizer alone does not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that a constrained reverse pass encourages dominant, reusable features and improves generalization across their tested classification, transfer, and generative settings. This conclusion does not establish any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a constrained reverse pass and a data-dependent reconstruction loss; compares against regular training and orthogonal regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: The MNIST result is reported after fine-tuning without regularization; the initial racecar-regularized phase has slightly lower performance than regular training. The text also reports different outcomes for racecar variants, including full and layer-wise constraints, but these do not measure the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: After fine-tuning without regularization, racecar-trained MNIST and 19-layer CIFAR-10 classifiers outperform the reported regular-training comparators. Racecar training initially reduces classification accuracy before fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Racecar regularization followed by fine-tuning can improve held-out image-classification accuracy relative to regular training.

record.problems: For the natural-image classification results summarized here, exact comparison values are presented only in figures or tables not numerically reproduced in the text. The paper does not report training-to-test gaps for these results.
record.rows_left_out: Transfer-learning results on CIFAR 10.1, CIFAR 100, n-MNIST, texture-shape, smoke, and stylization are omitted because they concern task transfer or changed data conditions, separate from the stated same-distribution claim. Feature and mutual-information measurements do not directly measure the listed versions.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate training data.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or local connectivity.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD under specified tuning budgets.
No controlled batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the experimental comparisons, not on the absence of training-to-test gaps: several listed versions can be tested using held-out performance alone.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch.
Tests racecar training and orthogonality regularization, not dropout.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measurement.

rows.subject: RRMNI
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on MNIST without regularization using RRmni as starting point
rows.operation_detail: Racecar training followed by fine-tuning without regularization; evaluated on the original MNIST task.
rows.baseline: StdMNI and OrtMNI; exact values not stated
rows.value: RRMNI outperforms OrtMNI and StdMNI; exact value figure only
rows.uncertainty: 5 repeated runs; exact uncertainty figure only
rows.note: The text says the result indicates racecar training yields generic features that can improve performance for the original task; it does not report the training-to-test gap.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with regular training and orthogonal regularization, so it should not be a claim-testing row. The reported post-fine-tuning advantage is supported by the prose, but measures no listed version. Numerical accuracies are referenced in Tables 3–4, whose contents are unavailable in the supplied extraction.

rows.subject: RRC10
rows.operation_detail: Racecar training followed by fine-tuning for CIFAR-10 classification.
rows.note: The text identifies this as natural-image classification, but gives no numeric accuracy in the supplied text and no train-to-test gap.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with regular training, so it should not be a claim-testing row. The reported post-fine-tuning advantage is supported by the prose, but measures no listed version. Numerical results are referenced in Table 5, whose contents are unavailable in the supplied extraction; '1/1' is not an accuracy result.
